question: Can I carry over unused sick days to next year?
answer: No. Unused sick days cannot be carried over into the next year, and they also cannot be paid out. You get up to 10 paid sick days each calendar year.

question: What is the daily allowance for a work trip to Ghana?
answer: A trip to Ghana is international travel, so the per diem is USD 60 per day. It covers meals and local incidentals and is paid for each night you spend away from home.

question: I'm in grade 6 and worked 5 extra approved hours last week. Will I get overtime pay?
answer: No. As a grade 6 employee you are not paid overtime; instead you receive time off in lieu (TOIL) at 1 hour off per approved extra hour, so your 5 approved hours earn you 5 hours of TOIL. You must use that TOIL within 2 months or it will be lost.

question: What is the hotel limit for an international trip?
answer: For international trips, hotels are capped at USD 180 per night. The only exception is when the Travel Desk confirms that no suitable option is available within that limit.

question: Can I work from Spain for two weeks while visiting family?
answer: Yes, potentially. You can work fully remotely for up to 2 weeks (10 working days) per calendar year, for example while visiting family. You need line manager approval in PeopleHub at least 5 working days in advance. Because Spain is outside Nigeria, you also need approval from People & Culture for tax and legal reasons.

question: I want to take a 4-day holiday. How far ahead must I request it?
answer: A 4-day holiday is more than 3 consecutive working days, so you must request it through the PeopleHub portal at least 10 working days in advance. Your leave is not confirmed until your line manager approves it in PeopleHub.

question: I'm a senior engineer (not a Director) flying 7 hours to London. Can I fly business class?
answer: No. Because your flight is longer than 6 hours but you are not Director level or above, you are not eligible for business class. You should travel premium economy where it is available, otherwise economy.
